data.name: Jainendra
data.gender_notes: Jainendra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jainendra is a Sanskrit name, derived from the words ‘jina’ meaning ‘victor’ and ‘indra’ meaning ‘lord’. This name is believed to signify a victorious and powerful lord. In Hindu mythology, Jainendra is also identified as Lord Indra, the god of rain, thunderbolts, and storms. The name Jainendra carries the meaning “God, Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jainendra usually hope their child will grow to embody god, lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of great spiritual significance, signifying divine victory and power.
data.etymology: Jainendra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God, Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jainendra total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Jainendra is a name with rich cultural significance in Indian tradition, representing power, victoriness, and royalty. Its association with Lord Indra, a central deity in Hinduism, further cements its importance within the cultural context. It encourages the bearer to hold sovereignty, exuding a sense of confidence and pride. The name is rooted in the ancient Indian culture and offers an intriguing blend of strength and elegance.
data.spiritual_significance: As the name Jainendra is derived from ‘jina’, meaning victor, it instills a sense of spiritual achievement, encouraging the individual to strive towards superiority over their personal struggles and negative tendencies. The name's spiritual significance can be traced back to the Jaina philosophies of self-discipline, non-violence, and renunciation. The name serves as a reminder to embrace spiritual journeys and aim for inner peace and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jainendra: Supreme Leader of Jains. Symbolizes spiritual strength, self-discipline, and enlightenment in the pursuit of Jain dharma.

historical_references.reference: Jainendra was a prominent Jain monk and scholar in the 12th century. He is known for his extensive commentaries on the Agama texts, which are considered the foundational scriptures of Jainism. His works helped in the revival and preservation of Jainism during the medieval period.
historical_references.context: Medieval period, Revival and preservation of Jainism.

historical_references.reference: Jainendra Swami was a 19th century Jain monk and leader who played a significant role in the establishment of the Jain Samaj, an organization which aimed to promote Jainism among the common people and help in the social and economic upliftment of the Jain community. He was also a prolific writer and speaker, and his works have had a lasting impact on Jain thought and practice.
historical_references.context: Establishment of Jain Samaj, promoting Jainism and social welfare among the Jain community.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Jainendra' is of Hindu origin, derived from the Jain religion. In modern contexts, this name is seen on various platforms. On Instagram, accounts with this name often feature inspirational quotes and images related to spirituality and Jainism. On Amazon, there are various products sold under the name, including clothing and books about Jainism. In politics, there have been notable figures with this name, such as Jainendra Prasad, who has been a member of the Indian Parliament, further increasing its popularity.
